To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the p16INK4A gene is a tumour suppressor gene, inactivation of which is a critical event in bronchial carcinogenesis and that the p16 gene is inactivated at early stages of carcinogenesis by hypermethylation.
p16INK4A point mutations are rather a late event, and that p16INKA hypermethylation is an early event in bronchial tumorigenesis.
p16 point mutations and p16 promoter hypermethylation were detected in lung cancer and preneoplastic bronchial lesions, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the p16INK4A gene and its protein product in human lung cancer.
the role of p16INK4A gene in the development of squamous cell carcinoma of the lung.
the development and validation of a new method for the detection of p16INK4A promoter methylation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p16INK4A promoter hypermethylation may be an early event in bronchial carcinogenesis, but it is not a prerequisite for malignant transformation.
p16 inactivation is not a critical event in lung tumourigenesis.
p16INK4A is an important tumour suppressor gene in lung carcinogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inactivation of p16 by point mutations and promoter methylation is an important step in the development of squamous cell carcinogenesis.
inactivation of p16INK4A by promoter methylation is a frequent and early event in lung carcinogenesis and that p16INK4 is a potential target for chemoprevention in the lung.
